plain_english: Now the fifth chapter. Arjuna said: O Krishna, you praise renunciation of actions and again yoga; tell me decisively which one of these two is better. The question of the doubtful one is: is renunciation primary, or yoga again?
sanskrit_cite: atha pañcamo'dhyāyaḥ   arjuna uvāca   saṃnyāsaṃ karmaṇāṃ kṛṣṇa | punaryogaṃ ca śaṃsasi | yacchreyānetayorekastaṃ me brūhi viniścitam | saṃnyāsaḥ pradhānaṃ punaryoga iti sasaṃśayasya praśnaḥ

plain_english: The blessed Lord said: Renunciation and action-yoga are both bestowers of the highest good; but of the two, action-yoga is superior to renunciation of action. Here renunciation and action are not declared as one; rather, both combined give the highest good. Without yoga, renunciation does not arise; such is the distinction of yoga.
sanskrit_cite: śrībhagavānuvāca   saṃnyāsaḥ karmayogaśca niḥśreyasakarāvubhau | tayostu  karmasaṃnyāsātkarmayogo viśiṣyate | saṃnyāsaḥ karma ca-nātraiko'bhihitaḥ apitu ubhau saṃmilitau  niḥśreyasaṃ dattaḥ | yogena vinā saṃnyāso na saṃbhavatīti  yogasya viśeṣaḥ

plain_english: The one to be known is the eternal renouncer who neither hates nor desires; free from opposites, O mighty-armed, he is easily released from bondage. Therefore he alone is the renouncer for all time, by whom desire and aversion of mind are renounced, because his intellect has gone beyond pairs such as anger and delusion; he is indeed easily freed.
sanskrit_cite: jñeyaḥ sa nityasaṃnyāsī yo na dveṣṭi na kāṅkṣati | nirdvandvo  hi mahābāho | sukhaṃ bandhādvimucyate | ataśca sa eva sārvakālikaḥ saṃnyāsī yena  manaso'bhilāṣapradveṣau saṃnyastau yato'sya  dvandvebhyaḥ-krodhamohādibhyo niṣkrāntā dhīḥ | sa sukhaṃ mucyata  eva

plain_english: Fools call sankhya and yoga separate, but the wise do not; one who abides rightly obtains the fruit of both.
sanskrit_cite: sāṅkhyayogau pṛthagbālāḥ pravadanti na paṇḍitāḥ | ekamapyāsthitaḥ samyagubhayorvindate phalam

plain_english: What sankhya attains yoga also reaches; one who sees both sees rightly, for these two are eternally connected and neither knowing nor yoga stands without the other.
sanskrit_cite: yatsāṅkhyaiḥ prāpyate sthānaṃ tadyogairanagamyate | ekaṃ  sāṅkhyaṃ ca yogaṃ ca yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati | idaṃ sāṃkhyam ayaṃ ca yogaḥ-iti na bhedaḥ | etau hi  nityasaṃbaddhau | jñānaṃ na yogena binā | yogo'pi na tena vineti | ata ekatvamanayoḥ

plain_english: Renunciation is hard without yoga, but a yoga-united sage attains brahman without delay; for yogis this is easily obtained, while without yoga it is painful.
sanskrit_cite: saṃnyāsastu mahābāho duḥkhamāptumayogataḥ | yogayukto munirbrahma  na cireṇādhigacchati | tuśabdo'vadhāraṇe bhinnakramaḥ | yogarahitasya saṃnyāsamāptuṃ  duḥkhameva-prāṅgītyā karmaṇāṃ duḥsaṃnyāsatvāt | yogibhistu  sulabhamevaitat-ityuktaṃ prāk

plain_english: Even while acting, one who is yoked to yoga, pure in self, master of self and senses, and whose self has become the self of all beings is not stained; likewise one whose self is the self of all beings, even while doing everything, is not stained, because of the elevated denial of the instruments of action.
sanskrit_cite: yogayukto viśuddhātmā vijitātmā jitendriyaḥ | sarvabhūtātmabhūtātmā kurvannapi na lipyate | sarvabhūtānāmātmabhūta atmā yasva sa sarvamapi kurvāṇo na  lipyate-karaṇapratiṣedhārūḍhatvāt

plain_english: The knower of truth, though yoked, would not think, 'I do nothing at all,' while perceiving, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, moving, breathing, and sleeping.
sanskrit_cite: naiva kiñcitkaromīti yukto manyeta tattvavit | paśyañśṛṇvanspṛśañjighrannaśnangacchanśvasansvapan

plain_english: Speaking, releasing, grasping, opening, and closing—even so, the senses function among sense-objects; holding thus.
sanskrit_cite: pralapanvisṛjangṛhṇannunmiṣannimiṣannapi | indriyāṇīndriyārtheṣu vartanta iti dhārayan

plain_english: One who places actions in Brahman and abandons attachment is not stained by sin, just as a lotus leaf is not wetted by water; therefore, even while performing acts such as seeing, one remains firm in realization, recognizes that the senses' activity in their own objects brings no personal result, and understands that another's deed does not stain another. Offering actions to Brahman is the sign of freedom from attachment, and so one is not stained.
sanskrit_cite: brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ | lipyate na  sa pāpena padmapatramivāmbhasā | ata eva darśanādīni kurvannapi asāvevaṃ  dhārayati-pratipattidārḍhyena  niścinute-cakṣurādīnāmindriyāṇāṃ yadi svaviṣayeṣu pravṛttiḥ  mama kimāyātam nahyanyakṛtena parasya lepaḥ-iti | tadeva brahmaṇi  karmaṇāṃ samarpaṇam | atra cihnamasya gatasaṃgatā | ato na lipyate

plain_english: Yogis perform actions through body, mind, intellect, and even the senses, having abandoned attachment for self-purification; and because attachment is absent, they act through these instruments as mutually independent and free from attachment.
sanskrit_cite: kāyena manasā buddhyā kevalairindriyairapi | yoginaḥ karma kurvanti  saṅgaṃ tyaktvā''tmaśuddhaye | yoginaśca kevalaiḥ-saṅgarahitaiḥ parasparānapekṣibhiśca  kāyādibhiḥ kurvanti karmāṇi saṅgābhāvāt

plain_english: The disciplined person, abandoning the fruit of action, attains final peace; the undisciplined person, acting from desire and attached to the fruit, is bound and does not return.
sanskrit_cite: yuktaḥ karmaphalaṃ tyaktvā śāntimāpnoti naiṣṭhikīm | ayuktaḥ  kāmakāreṇa phale sakto nibadhyate | naiṣṭhikīm-apunarāvartinīm

plain_english: Renouncing all actions by mind, the controlled embodied one sits happily in the nine-gated city, not acting or causing, just as a man inside a house is not affected by those in the house.
sanskrit_cite: sarvakarmāṇi manasā saṃnyasyāste sukhaṃ vaśīm | navadvāre pure  dehī naiva kurvanna kārayan | yathā veśmāntargatasya puṃso na gṛhagatairjīrṇatvādibhiryogaḥ  evaṃ mama cakṣurādicchidragavākṣanavakālaṅkṛtadehagehagatasya na  taddharmayogaḥ

plain_english: The lord does not create agency, actions, or union with fruit; nature proceeds. The self does nothing for anyone; its activity is only nature, not desire for fruit.
sanskrit_cite: na kartṛtvaṃ na karmāṇi lokasya sṛjati prabhuḥ | na  karmaphalasaṃyogaṃ svabhāvastu pravartate | eṣa ātmā na kiṃcitkasyacitkaroti | pravṛttistvasya  svabhāvamātraṃ na phalepsayā | tathāhi | saṃvedanātmano  bhagavataḥ prakāśānandasvātantryaparamārthasvabhāvasya  svabhāvamātrākṣiptasamastasṛṣṭisthitisaṃhṛtiprabandhasya  svasvabhāvānna manāgapyapāyo jātucit | iti na  kartravasthātiriktaṃ kartṛtvaṃ kiṃcit | tadabhāvātkāni karmāṇi  tad sattve kasya phalam ko vā karmaphalasaṃbandhaḥ | karmātra kriyā | karmaphalamapi ca kriyāphalameva | tathāhi | daṇḍacakraparivartanādikriyā nānyā | na ca sā  ghaṭaniṣpāditā-saṃvidantarvartitvāt | tasmāccetanaḥ svatantraḥ  parameśvara eva tathā tathā bhāti iti na tadvyatiriktaṃ  kriyātatphalādikamiti siddhāntaḥ

plain_english: The all-pervading lord takes no sin or merit; knowledge covered by ignorance deludes beings, and sin is done by their own ignorance.
sanskrit_cite: ata eva kriyātatphalayorabhāve vidhiphalasyāpi nādṛṣṭakṛtatā  kācit-ityardhenābhidhāyārdhāntareṇa saṃsāriṇaḥ prati  tatsamarthanaṃ kartumāha   nādatte kasyacit pāpaṃ na caiva sukṛtaṃ vibhuḥ | ajñānenāvṛtaṃ jñānaṃ tena muhyanti jantavaḥ | pāpādīni naitatkṛtāni | kintu nijenājñānena kṛtāni  śaṅkayevāmṛte viṣam

plain_english: By knowledge ignorance is destroyed; knowledge then manifests the supreme, self-manifest like the sun when darkness is gone.
sanskrit_cite: ata eva   jñānena tu tadajñānaṃ yeṣāṃ nāśitamātmanaḥ | teṣāmādityavajjñānaṃ prakāśayati tatparam | jñānena tu ajñāne nāśite jñānasya svaprakāśatvaṃ svataḥ  siddham yathā ādityasya tamasi naṣṭe | vinivartitāyāṃ hi  śaṅkāyāmamṛtamamṛtakāryaṃ svayameva karoti | tacca tadgatabuddhimanasāṃ tyaktānyavyāpārāṇāṃ  ghaṭate-ityāśayaṃ prakaṭayitu-māha-

plain_english: Those whose intellect and self are fixed there, devoted and focused, go to non-return, purified by knowledge from stain.
sanskrit_cite: tadbuddhayastadātmānastanniṣṭhāstatparāyaṇāḥ | gacchantyapunarāvṛttiṃ jñānanirdhautakalmaṣāḥ

plain_english: Even remembering and touching this, though attached in their own action, they do not stick in mud, like sun rays, because nature proceeds thus.
sanskrit_cite: smaranto'pi muhustvetatspṛśanto'pi svakarmaṇi | saktā api na  sajjanti paṅke ravikarā iva | yata evaṃ svabhāvastu pravartate iti ato dhvastājñānānāmitthaṃ  sthitirityāha-

plain_english: The wise see equally in brahmin, cow, elephant, dog, and outcaste, yet act appropriately; consciousness-nature is one in all bodies.
sanskrit_cite: vidyāvinayasampanne brāhmaṇe gavi hastini | śuni caiva śvapāke ca  paṇḍitāḥ samadarśinaḥ | tathā caḥ teṣāṃ yogināṃ brāhmaṇe nedṛśī buddhiḥ-asya  śuśrūṣādināhaṃ puṇyavānbhaviṣyāmi-ityādi | gavi na  pāvanīyamityādi | hastini nārthādidhīḥ | śuni  nāpavitrāpakāritādiniścayaḥ | śvapāke ca na  pāpāpavitrādidhiṣaṇā | ata eva samaṃ paśyantīti natu  vyavaharanti | yaduktaṃ   ciddharmā sarvadeheṣu viśeṣo nāsti kutracit | ataśca tanmayaṃ  sarvaṃ bhāvayanbhavajijjanaḥ | (vi0 bhai0 100)   iti atrāpi bhāvayanniti-jñānasyaiveyaṃ dhāroktā | tasya cetthaṃ saṃbhāvanetyāha-

plain_english: The steady, unconfused knower of brahman does not rejoice or grieve at gain; friend-enemy distinction is only convention.
sanskrit_cite: na prahṛṣyet priyaṃ prāpya nodvijetprāpya cāpriyam | sthirabuddhirasammūḍho brahmavid brahmaṇi sthitaḥ | etasya samadarśinaḥ śatrumitrādivibhāgo'pi vyavahāramātra eva  nāntaḥ-brahmaniṣṭhatvāt

plain_english: The self unattached to external contacts finds happiness in itself and enjoys imperishable happiness through brahman-yoga.
sanskrit_cite: bāhyasparśeṣvasaktātmā vindatyātmani yatsukham | sa  brahmayogayuktātmā sukhamavyamaśnute | bāhyasparśe viṣayātmani saktiryasya nāsti

plain_english: Contact-born enjoyments are pain-sources with beginning and end; the wise one does not delight in them.
sanskrit_cite: sa hyevaṃ manyate-ityāha   ye hi saṃsparśajā bhogā duḥkhayonaya eva te | ādyantavantaḥ  kaunteya na teṣu ramate budhaḥ | sa hyevaṃ bhāvayati-bāhyaviṣayajā bhogāḥ sarve  duḥkhakāraṇarūpāḥ tathāvidhā apyanityāḥ

plain_english: He who can endure the impulse of desire and anger before bodily release is disciplined and happy.
sanskrit_cite: śaknotīhaiva yaḥ soḍhuṃ prākśarīravimocanāt | kāmakrodhodbhavaṃ vegaṃ sa yuktaḥ sa sukhī mataḥ | na caitadduḥśakaṃ-śarīrāntakālaṃ yāvat krodhakāmajo vegaḥ  kṣaṇamātraṃ yadi sahyate tadā ātyantikī sukhaprāptiḥ

plain_english: He who is happy within, delighted within, and inner light attains supreme yoga as brahman-become.
sanskrit_cite: antaḥsukho'ntarārāmastathā'ntarjyotireva yaḥ | sa pārtha  paramaṃ yogaṃ brahmabhūto'dhigacchati | atastasyāntareva bāhyānapekṣi sukham tatraiva ramate | tatra cāsya  prakāśaḥ | vyavahāre tu mūḍhatvamiva | uktaṃ ca-jaḍa eva vica  redavādamatiḥ (pa0 sā0 71) iti

plain_english: Sages obtain brahmanirvāṇa when their stains are worn away, duality is cut, selves are restrained, they are devoted to the welfare of all beings, and the two knots of difference and doubt are destroyed.
sanskrit_cite: labhante brahmanirvāṇamṛṣayaḥ kṣīṇakalmaṣāḥ | chinnadvaidhā  yatātmānaḥ sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ | etacca taiḥ prāpyaṃ yeṣāṃ bhedasaṃśayarūpau granthī vinaṣṭau

plain_english: For ascetics freed from desire and anger, with controlled minds and known selves, brahmanirvāṇa is present on all sides; the ultimate existence of brahman in every state does not await a time of cessation.
sanskrit_cite: kāmakrodhavimuktānāṃ yatīnāṃ yatacetasām | abhito  brahmanirvāṇaṃ vartate viditātmanām | teṣāṃ sarvataḥ-sarvāsvavasthāsu brahmasattā pāramārthikī na  nirodhakālamapekṣate

plain_english: Having made contacts external and kept the eye within, one equalizes prāṇa and apāna, arranges all senses, establishes mind-activity in equality, and does not act crookedly; this alone is external.
sanskrit_cite: sparśānkṛtvā bahirbāhyāṃścakṣuścaivāntare bhruvoḥ | prāṇāpānau samau kṛtvā nāsābhyantaracāriṇau | bāhyasparśān bahiḥkṛtvā-anaṅgīkṛtya  bhruvoḥ-vāmadakṣiṇadṛṣṭyoḥ  krodharāgātmikayorantare-tadrahitesthānaviśeṣe  cakṣurūpalakṣitāni sarvendriyāṇi vidhāya  prāṇāpānau-dharmādharmau cittavṛttyabhyantare sāmyenāvasthāpya  nasate-kauṭilyenāsāmyena krodhādivaśādvyavaharati-iti nāsā  cittavṛttiḥ | etadeva bāhye

plain_english: A sage with restrained senses, mind, and intellect, devoted to liberation, whose desire, fear, and anger have departed, is always liberated; such a yogin, even while conducting all transactions, is indeed liberated.
sanskrit_cite: yatendriyamanobuddhirmunirmokṣaparāyaṇaḥ | vigatecchābhayakrodho  yaḥ sadā mukta eva saḥ | evaṃvidho yogī sarvavyavahārān vartayannapi mukta eva

plain_english: Knowing me as the enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities, great lord of all worlds, and friend of all beings, one attains peace; knowing such divine principle, one is liberated even while situated as is.
sanskrit_cite: bhoktāraṃ yajñatapasāṃ sarvalokamaheśvaram | suhṛdaṃ  sarvabhūtānāṃ jñātvā māṃ śāntimṛcchati | yajñaphaleṣu bhoktā-tyaktaphalatvāt | evaṃ tapaḥsu | īdṛśaṃ  bhagavattattvaṃ vidan yathātathāsthito'pi mucyata iti śivam

plain_english: Here is the summary verse: for one who sees all beings with equality, even conduct like the inert serves only for liberation.
sanskrit_cite: atra saṃgrahaślokaḥ   sarvāṇyevātra bhūtāni samatvenānupasyataḥ | jaḍavadvyavahāro'pi mokṣāyaivāvakalpate | iti  śrīmahāmāheśvarācāryavaryarājānakābhinavaguptapādaviracite  śrīmadbhagavadgītārthasaṃgrahe pañcamo'dhyāyaḥ
